theory.overview: A Segment Tree is a tree data structure for storing intervals, or segments. It allows querying which of the stored segments contain a given point, and finding the minimum/maximum/sum over a range in O(log n) time. It's a height-balanced binary tree representing an array, where each node stores information about a segment of the array. Segment trees are essential for range query problems that require both point updates and range queries.

keyConcepts.name: Tree Structure
keyConcepts.description: Leaf nodes represent individual array elements. Internal nodes represent ranges and store aggregates (sum, min, max).

keyConcepts.name: Build Operation
keyConcepts.description: Recursively build tree from array. O(n) time. Each node's value combines its children's values.

keyConcepts.name: Range Query
keyConcepts.description: Query aggregates over any range [l, r] by combining O(log n) relevant nodes that partition the range.

keyConcepts.name: Point Update
keyConcepts.description: Update a single element and propagate changes up the tree. O(log n) time by visiting nodes on path to root.
